intervals.label: conceptual design
intervals.quote: The Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO) is proposed to determine the neutrino mass hierarchy using an underground liquid scintillator detector.

intervals.label: civil construction of underground laboratory
intervals.note: The JUNO Collaboration's own Initial performance results paper (arXiv:2511.14590) gives this date directly.
intervals.quote: The civil construction of the JUNO underground lab started in January 2015.

intervals.label: detector installation (support structure, acrylic vessel, PMTs)
intervals.note: CORRECTED 2026-09-18: replaces the earlier single interval (start '2021', confidence approximate, sourced only to a search-engine summary) with day-precision dates verified directly in the JUNO Collaboration's own paper.
intervals.quote: The installation of the Stainless Steel support structure started on 19 December 2021 ... The installation of the photomultiplier tube (PMT) modules and electronics boxes started on 23 October 2022 and finished on 17 December 2024.

physics_goals.quote: the detection of reactor antineutrinos can resolve the neutrino mass hierarchy at a confidence level of 3-4σ
physics_goals.value: Determine the neutrino mass ordering using reactor antineutrinos

physics_goals.quote: determine neutrino oscillation parameters sin²θ₁₂, Δm²₂₁, and |Δm²ₑₑ| to an accuracy of better than 1%
physics_goals.value: Measure neutrino oscillation parameters sin²θ₁₂, Δm²₂₁ and |Δm²ₑₑ| to sub-percent precision

physics_goals.quote: observe supernova neutrinos, study the atmospheric, solar neutrinos and geo-neutrinos, and perform exotic searches
physics_goals.value: Study supernova, atmospheric, solar and geo-neutrinos and search for new physics

summary.plain: A giant underground detector in southern China that studies neutrinos from nearby nuclear power reactors. It began taking data in 2025 and aims to work out the ordering of neutrino masses and measure their oscillations with world-leading precision.
summary.technical: 20 kt liquid-scintillator reactor-antineutrino oscillation experiment 52.5 km from the Yangjiang and Taishan nuclear power plants, sited 700 m underground near Kaiping, Jiangmen, Guangdong. Aims to determine the neutrino mass ordering (3-4σ in 6 years) and measure sin²θ₁₂, Δm²₂₁ and |Δm²ₑₑ| to sub-percent precision; began physics data taking 2025-08-26.

unique_capabilities.note: The quote gives the simulated 'effective energy resolution' of 3.02%/√E (MeV) from the paper abstract (arXiv:2104.02565).
unique_capabilities.quote: we expect a yield of 1345 p.e. per MeV and an effective energy resolution of 3.02%/\sqrt{E (MeV)}$ in simulations
unique_capabilities.value: 20-kiloton liquid-scintillator central detector with sub-percent energy resolution, the largest such detector built to date
